pr_title: net: sockets: Fix SO_SNDTIMEO and SO_RCVBUF options
pr_body:
SO_SNDTIMEO socket option did not configure TX timeout on a socket properly. When testing the fix, it turned out that also SO_SNDBUF/SO_RCVBUF socket options were broken, not modifying the unerlying TCP window sizes properly.

This PR fixes the above issues. First two commits address the problem with SO_RCVBUF and adds new tests that verify that TCP windows are affected properly when changing SO_RCVBUF/SO_SNDBUF. 

The remaining commits, fix the TX timeouts on a socket, if configured, and add tests that verify this functinoality.

Fixes #55641

issue_context.title: Socket Timeout Ignored
comments:
@clamattia Very good catch.

Additionally, `timeout` in `send_check_and_wait` is ignored completely afterwards.
If it was `K_FOREVER`, however, then `buf_timeout` is used, which is a hard-coded to be 10 seconds.
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/net/lib/sockets/sockets.c#L664

As for civetweb, it's not because of Zephyr, it's more generic.
Also it's dropped, unfortunatelly, even though after couple of fixes in our fork of Civetweb (mainly thread fixes) and after fixes of POSIX in Zephyr it works perfectly fine for us.

If I read posix correctly, for `K_FOREVER` it is required to actually wait forever:

https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/send.html
"If space is not available at the sending socket to hold the message to be transmitted, and the socket file descriptor does not have O_NONBLOCK set, send() shall block until space is available. "

This is to cover the scenario when the application shrinks the max window when some communication is already ongoing. In this case, the new current new window size could fall below 0.
At the same time, if the application updates the window after consuming the data, immediately after shrinking the new window size could exceed the max window, hence extra check.
